entities.summary: The Ibuki class , also called the Kurama class , was a ship class of two large armoured cruisers built for the Imperial Japanese Navy after the Russo-Japanese War of 1904–1905. These ships reflected Japanese experiences during that war as they were designed to fight side-by-side with battleships and were given an armament equal to, or superior to existing Japanese battleships. The development of the battlecruiser the year before Ibuki was completed made her and her sister ship Kurama obsolete before they were completed because the foreign battlecruisers were much more heavily armed and faster.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Ibuki-class battlecruisers played a significant role in Japan's naval expansion and modernization following the Russo-Japanese War, but their design was ultimately rendered obsolete by foreign battlecruisers. The development of these ships influenced Japanese naval strategy and technology for decades to come.
